findings.summary: Pairing presses at RmlUi's pointer-lock filter was one level too shallow: every physical mouse release now ends SDL's capture request in both event drains (end_press_mouse_capture, before DOM listeners, the prevented-default continue and the UI filter), superseding both the per-button mask and a lock-entry SDL_CaptureMouse(false).

A prevented release withholds it from RmlUi too: minecraft's canvas contextmenu preventDefault on an unlocked right-click left SDL_CaptureMouse standing, which takes effect at once; the drain-level release covers it (cdb: SDL_CaptureMouse 1 then 0 for every press).

Delete the pressed-button mirror mask: it went stale on prevented releases and focus loss, and let a relative-mode release reach RmlUi when a listener locked during a UI press; the pointer-lock filter keeps its absolute rule and original comment.

A prevented release on the textarea resize grip left the resize running; the drains call a UI-installed DomInput::end_withheld_press, the grip's own SDL_CaptureMouse(false) is gone (the drains own the release), and the dom-input fixture asserts the hook.
State the capture fact once, at end_press_mouse_capture, instead of a six-line symptom narrative in the filter comment.
